newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Retevision to announce bidders on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Retevision to announce bidders on Wednesday.

text.p: Retevision, which will soon become Spain's second basic telephone operator, will announce early on Wednesday its decision on which groups may bid to purchase 60 percent of it, a spokeswoman told Reuter on Tuesday.
"The Retevision sale committee will meet tonight. We won't make a public announcement until early tomorrow," said the spokeswoman.

Industry sources expect that three different groups will be allowed to bid: Mannesmann and AT&T; a group including Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom, Sprint Corp and BCH ; and a group including Stet International, Endesa, Union Fenosa and Basque group Euskatel.
On April 25, Retevision said that Retevision sale committee would propose to the board that consortium Unisource's request to delay the deadline for presenting its candidacy be denied.

This means Unisource will not be allowed to present an independent bid for the 60 percent stake in Retevision that the state is selling, although it will be allowed to join its effort with the other three groups of bidders.
Unisource is a consortium of telecoms flagships from the Netherlands, Switzerland and Sweden and is led by AT&T.
